root.name: King's Indian Defense: Fianchetto Variation, Immediate Fianchetto

overview: White fianchettoes the king's bishop and keeps the centre flexible instead of building the big e4 centre. Black normally reaches the King's Indian set-up with ...Bg7, ...d6, ...O-O and ...Nc6 or ...Nbd7, then plays ...e5 or ...c6 or ...a6 and ...Rb8 for queenside play. The game is slower and less tactical than the Classical or Sämisch: White squeezes with Nc3, Nf3, O-O and e4, Black looks for ...e5 or ...c5 counterplay.

white_ideas.idea: Bg2, Nc3, Nf3, O-O, then e4 to build a centre behind the fianchetto
Pressure on the long diagonal and the d5 and e5 squares
Queenside play with b4 and c5 or Rb1 against ...a6 and ...Rb8

black_ideas.idea: Fianchetto the king's bishop and castle, then challenge the centre with ...e5
...c6 and ...Qa5 or ...Nbd7 and ...e5 for a flexible set-up

typical_structures.structure: King's Indian pawn chain with Black pawns on d6 and e5 against White c4 and d4/d5
Closed centre after d5 with ...e6 or ...c6, play on the wings

character.notes: Fianchetto KID is positional with less kingside-attack danger than the Classical or Sämisch; both kings are safe. Not forcing early.

soundness.notes: Fully sound; a main line at elite level.

structure.notes: Centre often held in tension with c4 and d4 versus ...d6 and ...e5; may close with d5 later. Flexible, not decided.

approach.notes: Standard branch of the King's Indian, not a universal system.

level.notes: Plans matter more than move orders, but nothing needs long forced lines. Intermediate.

sublines_that_differ.name: Fianchetto with ...c6
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 Bg7 4. Nf3 d6 5. g3 O-O 6. Bg2 c6
sublines_that_differ.how: Quieter, Black avoids ...e5 commitments and often plays ...Qa5.

sublines_that_differ.name: Fianchetto with ...Nc6
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 Bg7 4. Nf3 d6 5. g3 O-O 6. Bg2 Nc6 7. O-O a6
sublines_that_differ.how: Black plays ...Rb8 and ...b5 on the queenside; a bit sharper.

character.reason: Positional squeeze against ...e5 counterplay, neither forcing nor especially hard to crack.

soundness.reason: A main-line system at the top level.

structure.reason: Centre stays in tension and may or may not close with d5.

approach.reason: A normal choice against the King's Indian, not a system.

plans.reason: Both bishops on the long diagonals and play on the queenside.
